Definition: from G3366 and G4218; not even ever:--never.
BiblicalUsage: The word means never, not even ever, and Paul uses it once, of the men of the last days: ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the verse is a warning about learning without truth: a man can study for ever and never arrive, if he will not submit to what he learns.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
